title: Classic Crème Caramel
summary: Silky individual custards of milk, cream and eggs baked gently over a dark caramel, chilled and turned out so the caramel runs down as a sauce.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the caramel
steps.text: Put the sugar, water and lemon juice in the light-coloured pan and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat without stirring, brushing down the sides with a wet brush. Boil, swirling the pan now and then, for 10-13 min until the syrup is a deep honey-amber. A pale pan lets you judge the colour; stop before it smokes or it will taste bitter.

steps.title: Coat the ramekins
steps.text: Pour the caramel straight into the ramekins and tilt each one so the base is covered. Leave them for 15 min so the caramel hardens before the custard goes in.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Heat the oven to 165 °C (145 °C fan). Warm the milk and cream in the second pan for about 6 min until steaming. Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar only until combined, then whisk in the hot milk, vanilla and salt gently so you do not raise foam, and strain into the jug.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Lay the tea towel in the roasting tin and set the ramekins on it, then fill them with custard. Pour boiling water into the tin to halfway up the ramekins, cover the tin loosely with foil and bake for 35-45 min. They are done when a knife pushed in halfway between the centre and edge comes out clean and the centre reads about 80 °C; the towel stops the bases overheating.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cool the ramekins on a rack for 30 min, then cover and chill for at least 4 h. This long rest also lets the hard caramel dissolve into a sauce.

steps.title: Turn out
steps.text: Run the palette knife round each custard, put a plate over the top and flip it over. Give a gentle shake so the custard drops out with all its caramel.

tips: The most common mistake is boiling the custard mixture or baking too hot, which leaves the custard full of holes; keep the oven at 165 °C and the water bath topped up.
Swirl rather than stir the caramel, as a spoon can make it crystallise.
Soak the caramel pan in hot water and it will clean itself.
Make them a day ahead: the caramel turns into more sauce overnight.
storage: Keep covered in the ramekins in the fridge for up to 2 days and turn out just before serving. Not suitable for freezing.
